data.exact_reserve_text: Within the calendar year net technical result, deficit of GBP 2.2m on direct business (2020: surplus of GBP 1.0m) and deficit of GBP 42.6m on reinsurance accepted business (2020: surplus of GBP 2.5m) relate to the reassessment of net claims incurred for previous accident years. The GBP 42.6m deficit is primarily due to material uncertainty arising from a potential accumulation of claims in respect of a single policyholder. The claims in question are very complex, due to uncertainty over coverage, liability and the quantum of the claims. A large material outstanding claims technical provision has been established for potential claims and expenses related to this matter but depending upon the legal outcome of these various factors this reserve may be significantly higher or lower than the outstanding claims provision established. This uncertainty is beyond the usual level of uncertainties within outstanding claims provisions.

prior_year_events.event_name: Accumulation of claims by single policyholder
prior_year_events.impact_description: Material uncertainty and adverse development arising from a potential accumulation of claims in respect of a single policyholder; complex coverage/liability issues led to a large outstanding claims provision being established.

data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims outstanding increased from GBP 206.4m at 1 Jan 2021 to GBP 221.9m at 31 Dec 2021. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle indicates a net prior year strengthening of approximately GBP 14.7m (about 7.1% of opening gross claims). The adverse movement was driven by large loss development and a material accumulation of claims associated with a single policyholder (complex coverage and liability issues), with knock-on effects on recoveries and reinsurance arrangements.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development (gross) was derived from the published gross claims development triangle (figures shown in GBP '000) because there is no explicit single-line gross 'Movement in prior year's provision' in the notes. The triangle may be influenced by intra-group RITC/LPT transactions (notably transfers referenced elsewhere in the report) and reinsurance transfers; narrative figures quoted in the report are often net of reinsurance, so net and gross measures differ. The triangle was used as the primary source for gross PYD; this may under/over-state impacts where RITC or acquired portfolios changed the vintage profiles.
